clue.text: Right person always producing sacred word in general

indicators.note: the sacred syllable is placed within the commander's surname

parts.note: George Custer was the US cavalry general of Little Bighorn
Om is the sacred syllable chanted in Hindu and Buddhist practice

explanation.surface: A preacher's text about someone always in the right, uttered by a holy word amid the general crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the shop saying that the buyer is always right.
explanation.definitionFit: The retail maxim says the shopper is always right, so the 'right person always' is the shop's client.

clue.text: Sark boatless, Jersey or Guernsey getting boat

indicators.note: the island's name loses a word for a vessel, Noah's being the obvious one

parts.note: both are breeds of dairy cattle named after Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Without boats on Sark, someone from Jersey or Guernsey picks up a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Sark, Jersey and Guernsey are all Channel Islands, which makes the cattle breeds look like places. 'boatless' takes ARK out of SARK, leaving S.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed barge used for freight is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Vulnerable spot for church

definitions.meaning: the side of the head, where a blow can be dangerous

explanation.definitionFit: The thin side of the skull is a weak point, and a place of worship is another sense of the same word.

clue.text: Save more pants!

definitions.meaning: consume a smaller amount, read as two words
British slang for rubbish or worthless

explanation.definitionFit: Split into two words it means to consume less; whole it means worthless, which British slang calls 'pants'.

clue.text: Situation as nice or nasty

indicators.note: these letters are given a nasty treatment and messed about

explanation.surface: A scenario offered as either a nice one or a nasty one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges the eight letters of AS NICE OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A projected sequence of events or setting is a situation in synonym terms.

clue.text: Poetry written about a hostile French city

indicators.note: the lines of poetry are written round the other pieces

parts.note: verses are lines of poetry
ill as in ill will, unfriendly

explanation.surface: A poem composed about an unfriendly city in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hostile' is ILL as in ill will; 'written about' wraps the poetry word around A and ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: The palace town south-west of Paris is a city in France.

clue.text: Plant's gender almost identical

indicators.note: the word for gender loses its final letter

parts.note: sex is a synonym for gender
same means identical

explanation.surface: A botanical note that a plant's gender is all but the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilseed herb grown for its seeds is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Sonny didn't tremble ___ , in view of East London?

definitions.meaning: the gap completes Sonny didn't tremble ... 'ook, a Cockney 'shook' for the pop duo Sonny and Cher

explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang a look rhymes with this phrase, so it means a glance or view.

clue.text: Able to get a handle on calculus, initially

indicators.note: on puts the calculus letter in front, the handle being tacked on after it
only the opening letter of the maths word is used

parts.note: a lever is a handle for operating machinery

explanation.surface: Someone able to get a grip on calculus at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever and able are synonyms for being capable or bright.

clue.text: Lather moistens back

indicators.note: the word for moistens is read from right to left

parts.note: wets means moistens

explanation.surface: Soapy foam dampens someone's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lather' is not soap suds but a state of agitation; 'back' turns WETS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a lather means being in a fluster, a state of anxious agitation.

clue.text: Islander mangling soapy linen

indicators.note: a mangle crushes laundry, so the letters are crushed and reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone from an island putting soapy linen through a mangle.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Pacific island group east of Melanesia is an islander.

clue.text: Bird collecting rent, returned over counter?

indicators.note: the whole assembled piece is turned back to front
the bird takes the tear inside itself

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
a rent is a rip or tear

explanation.surface: A bird gathering the rent and handing it back over the shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' and 'returned' build the bird-and-tear piece and turn it round. The question mark flags a playful definition: the cricket official counts the balls in each over.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket official counts the balls in each over, so a match official can be whimsically called one who counts.

clue.text: Unstable trio given a brace

indicators.note: the letters are unsteady and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A wobbly trio is handed a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brace' looks like a pair, but it is a verb, to fortify. 'Unstable' rearranges TRIO GIVEN A.
explanation.definitionFit: To brace someone is to refresh or strengthen them, a synonym for enlivening.

clue.text: Shoes back to front, one full of holes

indicators.note: the last letter of the footwear word is brought to the start

parts.note: trainers are sports shoes

explanation.surface: Shoes worn the wrong way round, one of them riddled with holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the final S of TRAINERS to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A sieve or colander is perforated all over, so it is something full of holes.

clue.text: Most adventurous combination of underclothes

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment
a vest is a British undershirt

explanation.surface: The most daring combination of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a VEST is the sleeveless undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: The most courageous person is the one most willing to take risks, the most adventurous.

clue.text: Avoid passage for vehicle

parts.note: to skip something is to avoid it
a lane is a narrow passage

explanation.surface: Steer clear of a passage meant for traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft fitted with skis for snow landings is a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Double letter with double letters spelled out as "fraud"

parts.note: W is spoken as 'double u', a doubled letter

indicators.note: the letters of the second word are set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A word with two pairs of letters written out, used as a term for a con man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters spelled out' rearranges DOUBLE to OULDBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender or wannabe claims a status they lack, so is a kind of fraud.

clue.text: Bad quality expensive jewellery? That's clumsy

parts.note: bum as an adjective means poor or worthless
bling is flashy, costly jewellery

explanation.surface: Wearing cheap-looking pricey jewellery is a clumsy look.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone awkward and inept is blundering about, the synonym being clumsy.

clue.text: Poet right to pen first of sonnets in support of sweetheart

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits beneath the first, holding it up

parts.note: the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

indicators.note: the opening letter is enclosed as if in a pen

parts.note: legit is slang for legitimate, right

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the poems' name is taken

explanation.surface: A poet rightly writing sonnets for his sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is the centre of sweet, E. 'to pen' puts S, picked by 'first of', inside LEGIT, and 'in support of' puts that below E.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of mournful verses for the dead is a kind of poet.

clue.text: Company of smokers inhaling good pile of poo

indicators.note: the tobacco firm breathes in the other letter

parts.note: Dunhill is a British tobacco and pipe company

explanation.surface: Smokers' firm breathing in a good heap of excrement.
explanation.definitionFit: A heap of manure is a pile of excrement, the clue's 'poo'.

clue.text: Planet where anyone can see river close to a canal

parts.note: U is the British film rating for universal viewing
the bodily opening at the end of the alimentary canal

explanation.surface: A planet visible to all, near a river by a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British cinema certificate meaning suitable for all ages. The 'canal' is not a waterway but the alimentary canal.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh world from the Sun is one of the planets.

clue.text: Full-bodied burgundy offered for starters? Very well!

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
my! and well! are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A wine waiter offers a big burgundy as a first course and the guest approves.
explanation.definitionFit: A buxom, ample-chested figure is full-bodied.

clue.text: Give away chance to get some sun

parts.note: a bet is a chance or gamble
a ray is a beam, some of the sun's light

explanation.surface: Throw away the chance to catch a bit of sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray is to reveal or let slip a secret, to give it away.

clue.text: Loud and doubly buoyant, one decorating Christmas tree

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
airy means light-hearted, buoyant
light means buoyant, as in light-hearted

explanation.surface: A loud and very cheerful person who decorates the Christmas tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' asks for two words for buoyant.
explanation.definitionFit: A small electric bulb on a string is hung on a festive tree as a decoration.

clue.text: Shell port

definitions.meaning: the outer casing of a ship, or a husk of seeds
the Yorkshire port on the Humber estuary

explanation.definitionFit: The outer casing of a boat is its shell, and the city on the Humber is an English port.

clue.text: See 8
Dog mounting sheep

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog
on, as in on top of something

explanation.surface: A dog getting on top of a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: The meat of a mature sheep, and by extension the animal, goes by this name.

clue.text: Marine gets to tell about end of voyage in the past

indicators.note: the word for tell goes round the others

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing, telling on someone

indicators.note: only the final letter of the journey word is taken

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A marine gets to recount the end of a voyage long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tell' is slang for informing on someone, as a grass sings to the police; 'about' wraps it round the voyage's final letter and the word for 'in the past'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ocean-going and marine both describe things belonging to the sea.
